title: Bar
description: One OHLCV bar state for one (provider, symbol, side, timeframe), as published to bars.{timeframe}.{provider}.{symbol}. Every bar window produces exactly two records, one per price side, published together; `side` is a field rather than a stream-name segment. Published on every intrabar update and once more at close; is_closed distinguishes the two. This file is the authority every implementation conforms to (tqtk-common in Python, a future Java adapter); neither is the contract itself. Timestamps are integer microseconds since the Unix epoch, UTC. Unknown fields are permitted so a producer can add a field before every consumer has adopted it.

provider.description: Data source whose ticks this bar was built from. Appears verbatim in the stream name bars.{timeframe}.{provider}.{symbol}, so it may not contain the '.' or ':' used as separators. Bars from different providers are never blended.

symbol.description: Canonical pipeline symbol, identical to the Tick field of the same name.

side.description: Which price of the tick this bar's OHLC was built from. A bar is a bid series or an ask series: every window produces one record per side, carrying the same tick_count since every tick supplies both. The enum is closed at two — a mid-price series is derivable by consumers and is never published as a third side.

timeframe.description: Bar width. The eight timeframes are fixed by the bar-aggregation capability: every tick updates the forming bar on all of them, on both sides.

bar_start_ts.description: Inclusive start of the bar's window, in microseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC), aligned to the timeframe boundary. Buckets are computed from the tick's recv_ts (event time), not arrival order. Alignment is not expressible in JSON Schema and is asserted by the implementations. With (provider, symbol, side, timeframe) this is the bar's identity: bar-persistence upserts on that tuple, and a consumer pairs a window's two sides on it.

open.description: First price folded into the window, on this record's side.

high.description: Highest price folded into the window, on this record's side. Expected to be >= max(open, close) and >= low; the relations are not expressible in JSON Schema and are asserted by the implementations.

low.description: Lowest price folded into the window, on this record's side. Expected to be <= min(open, close).

close.description: Most recent price folded into the window, on this record's side: the last price for a closed bar, the current price for a forming one.

tick_count.description: Ticks folded into the window so far, identical on the window's two side-records since every tick carries both a bid and an ask. 0 identifies an idle bar, carried forward as open = high = low = close = that same side's previous bar close, so that every series stays gapless.

is_closed.description: false while the bar is still forming, true once its grace-delayed close has fired. Only closed bars are persisted; a consumer must not treat a forming bar as final.

last_update_ts.description: recv_ts of the most recent tick folded into this bar, in microseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC). For an idle bar, the close event's own timestamp. Always >= bar_start_ts.
